title: The Ghost of Joseph Priestley
summary: An AI-powered interactive installation where visitors converse with the ghost of 18th-century scientist Joseph Priestley through a diary-based interface.

blocks.text: An AI-powered interactive experience bringing 18th-century scientist Joseph Priestley to life. Joseph Priestley discovered oxygen, invented carbonated water, and befriended Benjamin Franklin before fleeing England for revolutionary America. Yet most people have never heard of him.

This project creates an entertaining, portable installation where visitors converse with Priestley's "ghost" through a diary-based interface. Using LLM technology, the experience is designed for the Priestley-Forsyth Memorial Library in Northumberland, PA, and travels to schools and conferences, sparking curiosity about Priestley as a person.

title: Cavern GP
role: Programmer, Game Designer, Artist & Sound Designer
summary: A massive local multiplayer racing game for the Cavern — a 270° curved projection screen at CMU's Entertainment Technology Center — where the crowd cheers drivers into overtakes, crashes and fast corners.

blocks.text: Team 270° Fun developed a massive local multiplayer racing game focused on building community through sports. Designed for the Cavern system at the Entertainment Technology Center (ETC), the project utilizes the Cavern, a 270° curved projection screen and a 20-foot-wide interactive play area, enabling dynamic local multiplayer interactions within virtual environments.

The project's goal is to find a balance between having player agency and still feeling like part of the audience. Players work together as cheerleaders and fans, cheering for their favorite teams, affecting the drivers' behavior and causing overtakes, crashes, and fast cornering. This teamwork evokes a sense of belonging, deepening players' relationship with others supporting the same team.
The game was played at the ETC 2025 Fall Festival and received massive positive reviews. It also broke the record for the largest number of players in the Cavern — from 6 to 26.

I was mainly responsible for programming, game design, UI/UX, and sound design. My specific approach to each of those features can be found in the [documentation](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fZHUSGTnWkFYrxo2k6uY9g8hPcA-_BCsDHzC8WvrAdU/edit?usp=sharing).

blocks.text: Highlights
Waypoint System

The waypoint system guides cars along track paths with player-influenced speed, while lane switching enables overtakes, crashes and drifting. Designers can adjust it right inside the Unity Editor, which helped us build out the pipeline.
Mobile Controller

The mobile controller system lets players use their phones as real-time input devices to control the in-game vehicles. It connects Unity with external devices through a Node.js server, using HTML and JavaScript interfaces for seamless interaction — enabling multiplayer gameplay without additional hardware, and an easily customizable input layer for future projects.

items: Real-time synchronization between mobile browsers and Unity
Flexible, web-based input interface for rapid testing and iteration
Fully local, low-latency communication via Node.js server

title: The Tale of Oath
summary: A third-person, magic-based action-adventure set in Rifts England — a level design vertical slice from CMU's Entertainment Technology Center, now on Steam.

blocks.text: The Tale of Oath is a third-person action-adventure level design project from Carnegie Mellon University's Entertainment Technology Center, set in the Rifts Universe and bringing players into the mystical landscapes of Rifts England. The project centers on a magic-based adventure that emphasizes exploration, puzzle-solving, and world immersion.

The goal was to deliver a playable vertical slice that showcases the game's core mechanics — magic casting, environmental navigation, narrative worldbuilding, and Druid rescue — as a polished, self-contained experience. The game is now on [Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/3900080/The_Tale_of_Oath/).

I was mainly responsible for gameplay programming, VFX, and music. My specific approach to each can be found in the [documentation](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1LghiPeTN8Bva14sz1xjvyhQPLn83Leh4Is_4JOvyXB8/edit?usp=sharing).

title: Mento Issue
role: Game Designer, Programmer, Artist & Sound Designer
summary: A Global Game Jam 2025 game on the theme "Bubble", built around the reaction between Mentos and soda — winner of the Non-Traditional Award at GGJ Pittsburgh.

blocks.text: Yen-Chun Huang, Jack Peng, Alex Hall, and I attended the Global Game Jam Pittsburgh. The theme of the jam was "bubbles," which inspired us to create a game based on the reaction between Mentos and soda. Our concept was well received by the audience, earning us the Non-Traditional Award at the event.

Players control half a pack of Mentiez (a Mentos-like candy) with the ability to throw mints. The goal is to reunite with the other half of the pack — but the only way to navigate the map is by using Mentos to trigger special bubble effects from sodas.
The first version of the game is available on both [itch.io](https://yenchun.itch.io/mento-issue) and the GGJ website. Feel free to check it out and enjoy a piece of Mentiez!

blocks.text: Barr VR
October 2024 · Game Designer, Artist & Sound Designer

A VR game focused on throwing and dodging, made with programmers and artists — my first attempt at VR development, and an invaluable experience. Gameplay revolves around a card-drawing mechanic: both the player and the enemy draw cards to determine who throws and who dodges. Draw high, and you have 15 seconds to throw bottles at the enemy using the VR controllers, specifically tuned for a better throwing feel. Draw low, and the enemy takes their turn while you dodge projectiles using physical movement.

blocks.text: Lizard Boom!
November 2024 · Game Designer, Programmer & Sound Designer

A multiplayer game using eye trackers and adaptive controllers. Each round, a bomb spawns on a random player, who has to pass it on to survive. The eye tracker steers how each player moves around the map, and the buttons on the adaptive controllers punch and pass the bomb.

blocks.text: Shell Yeah!
November 2024 · Game Designer, Programmer, Artist & Sound Designer

A 4-player adaptation of Red Light, Green Light, made with one programmer and two artists. Three players steer crabs using foot pedals, while the fourth plays the Octopus on the Xbox Adaptive Controller, holding a button to fire a laser at them. Like a rhythm game, the crabs follow UI prompts on the pedals to move faster and escape the laser — and holding every button at once hides them inside a can, blocking it entirely.

title: Baller
summary: A class project built around a game of catch between two people — every time the ball is caught, a small part of the gameplay changes.

blocks.text: Baller is a class project based around the idea of playing a game of catch with two people. Each time the ball is caught, a small part of the gameplay changes. The concept was designed to keep the scope low, and to be easily expandable.
